title: Put your habits where you can see them
description: Visible reminders beat good intentions: place the objects of a habit in your path and let your eyes do the prompting.

body.heading: Out of sight really is out of mind
paragraphs: Most habits do not fail because we decide against them. They fail because the moment passes unnoticed. The vitamins stay in the cupboard, the journal stays in the drawer, and the day ends before we remember either.
Visibility is the simplest fix. What you see at the right moment, you are far more likely to do.

body.heading: Place the cue in the path of your day
paragraphs: Put the thing where the habit should happen, not where it is stored tidily. The yoga mat unrolled by the bed. The book on the pillow, not the shelf. The running shoes directly in front of the door you leave by.

It helps to pair the object with the moment: the water bottle next to the kettle you use every morning, the letter you need to post leaning against the front door. The cue works because it appears exactly when action is possible.

body.heading: Tidy cues still work
paragraphs: If visual clutter bothers you, use a single “habit spot” instead: one tray, basket or shelf corner where the current habit’s things live together. Everything in that spot is a gentle instruction.
When a habit becomes automatic, the cue can retire. Until then, let your surroundings remember for you — they are happy to, and they never get tired.

takeaway: If you keep forgetting a habit, do not try harder — put it where you will trip over it.
